text:
elaine: Quick convo: how should we handle dynamic units & tick formatting on the dashboard charts? Two pain points: 1) CPU/ops charts show huge numbers (e.g., 512000) that are unreadable without a unit transform, 2) latency charts sometimes switch between ms/s depending on zoom and that confuses folks.

ryan: +1 — we should auto-scale units (ms -> s, bytes -> KB/MB) but signpost it clearly. I prefer an SI suffix approach (e.g., 512k, 1.2M) and a small unit label next to the axis title like "Requests (1k)" that shows the scale factor.

vik: UX warning: implicit scaling can break exactness. For ops counts, people often copy values into alerts. We should offer a hover/click to show the exact raw number, not just the formatted one. Also when switching units on zoom, animate the tick labels so users notice the change.

mae: Accessibility: unit labels need to be included in the readable axis name for screen readers. Example aria-label: "Y axis: Requests per minute, units scaled to thousands (1k)"
